Zhang2021.title: Electrochemical properties of the non-excitable tissue stria vascularis of the mammalian cochlea are sensitive to sounds
Zhang2021.notes: Direct in-vivo microelectrode recording of intrastrial space potential (ISP) and marginal cell potential during acoustic stimulation (60-100 dB SPL). Shows immediate drop in ISP (Delta ISP ~ -2 to -4 mV) at sound onset due to hair-cell circulation current load.

Su2020.title: Furosemide prevents noise-induced hearing loss and enhances the preventive effect of N-acetylcysteine
Su2020.authors: Hongguo Su, Fan Wu, Khujista Haque, and Su-Hua Sha
Su2020.notes: In-vivo pre-exposure furosemide (50 mg/kg IP) transiently collapses EP, reducing hair-cell transduction driving force (V - E_MET) and metabolic strain during 106 dB SPL noise, preventing permanent hearing loss.

Marcus2002.title: Kcnj10 (Kir4.1) potassium channel knockout abolishes endocochlear potential
Marcus2002.notes: Kir4.1 channel knockout in-vivo: homozygous Kcnj10-/- mice exhibit EP = +1.8 +- 0.8 mV (vs +82.5 mV in WT), establishing Kir4.1 as the sole generator of the intermediate-cell diffusion potential.

Hou2020.title: Acoustic Trauma Causes Cochlear Pericyte-to-Myofibroblast-Like Cell Transformation and Vascular Degeneration, and Transplantation of New Pericytes Prevents Vascular Atrophy
Hou2020.authors: Zhiqiang Hou, Lingling Neng, Jinhui Zhang, Jing Cai, Xiaohan Wang, Yunpei Zhang, Ivan A. Lopez, and Xiaorui Shi
Hou2020.notes: In-vivo acoustic trauma (120 dB SPL) causes strial capillary pericyte transformation into contractile myofibroblasts, basement membrane thickening, capillary regression, and EP depression; pericyte transplantation rescues capillary density and EP.

coverage_notes: All identifiable EP timecourse panels from the seven requested drug articles are represented. Duplicate Ikeda 50 mg/kg control and related Japanese Ito curves are not counted twice.
No dose-response endpoints, age trajectories, auditory-threshold curves, potassium curves, or histological measurements are mislabeled as EP timecourses.
Interventions not represented by the current model are compiled but excluded from parameter estimation by user choice.

Noise cohorts retain discrete sampling and protocol metadata; absolute EP is not invented for vertically offset delta-EP traces. Cross-sectional injury data are compiled but are not mistaken for longitudinal acute recordings.

research_evidence.description: Canonical curated research evidence: scalar calibration observations, additional primary-study constraints, published experiment timing, and noise outcome context. Original study PDFs remain external source files referenced by SHA-256 in sources.

scalar_calibration.description: Curated scalar experimental constraints, not simulation output or copies of full-text articles.

Telang2010.preparation: C57BL/6 mouse pilot; ATP 100 uM, 10 nL, no PPADS

limitations: Reduction is approximate visual reading; whiskers approximately 26-39 mV have unspecified statistical meaning.

Nadir and recovery are narrative constraints, not digitized time-series measurements.
Recovery within 5 mV is a declared model criterion.

limitations: Converted from reported nM to uM.
One endpoint cannot identify release and clearance independently.
Bulk sampled ATP may not equal local receptor ATP; acoustic mapping unmeasured.

limitations: No verified EP amplitude, raw time course or uncertainty.

Morphology is not a calibrated measure of intrastrial volume.

Zhang2021.role: Validation of intrastrial space potential (V_IS / E_Kir) and sound-evoked circulation current load

Su2020.source: In-vivo pharmacological and noise challenge, Hear Res 395:108034 (2020)

Su2020.phenotype: Furosemide pre-treatment transiently suppresses EP, attenuating hair-cell transduction driving force (V - E_MET) and preventing permanent threshold shift (PTS)
Su2020.role: Validation of unified electrodynamic coupling between strial battery voltage and hair-cell metabolic load

Marcus2002.source: In-vivo microelectrode electrophysiology, Am J Physiol Cell Physiol 282:C403-C407 (2002)
Marcus2002.preparation: Kcnj10 null (Kir4.1 -/-) mice vs WT littermates

Hou2020.preparation: Guinea pigs and mice exposed to 120 dB SPL acoustic trauma
Hou2020.phenotype: Pericyte transformation (NG2+ to alpha-SMA+), strial capillary constriction, basement membrane thickening, and EP rundown; pericyte transplantation rescues capillary density and EP
Hou2020.role: Cellular and microvascular justification for trauma equation (W_trauma) and V1 deficit state

furosemide.interpretation: Only scale 1 is calibrated. Other scales are local-exposure sensitivity tests, not validated administered doses.

noise.source_locations: Fig. 1 (30-min exposure); Fig. 2A (10, 40, 110-min observations during sustained exposure)
published_conditions: 30 min, 85 dB SPL, closed-field 8-16 kHz band-pass noise
85 dB SPL, closed-field 4-32 kHz noise; ABR sampled at 10, 40, 110 min during exposure
noise.interpretation: M=4 is an exploratory load, not a conversion from 85 dB. P2X2_disabled sets maximal shunt conductance to zero only; it is not a developmental knockout model. Frequency selectivity and ABR/DPOAE are not modeled.

noise_evidence.preparation: 85 dB SPL, closed-field 4-32 kHz broadband noise

post_30min.location: Results associated with Fig. 2B, immediate post-exposure TTS

limitations: ABR threshold shift is not EP reduction; no unit conversion is supported.
C-model load multipliers are not calibrated equivalents of 85 dB SPL.
C-model shunt ablation is not a full developmental knockout.
Broadband Fig. 2B evidence is contextual for the 30-minute simulation, not a frequency-matched replication of the Fig. 1 octave-band protocol.

protocol_review.method: Each figure-level experiment has a normalized protocol_summary. Study-level route, species, strain, anesthesia, timing, dose, co-interventions and source notes remain under sources/experiments.
protocol_review.fit_rule: Fit only when the intervention is represented by the current model; unsupported exposure units, frequency-specific protocols, injury, genetic interventions and co-treatments remain evidence-only.
protocol_review.dose_duration_rule: Reported and assumed infusion durations are kept distinct in duration_evidence; assumptions are not promoted to reported measurements.
